chunks: Sayyid Murtadha (may Allah have mercy on him) said at the end:

It is not impossible that there are many matters here that have not reached us, which are entrusted with the Imam (peace be upon him), and although the narrators have concealed them and not transmitted them,
it does not follow from that that the religious obligation falls away from the people.
Because if the reason for the occultation is his fear for his life from those who threatened him,
the one who forced him to hide is responsible for the loss of what is lost from the Sharia (religious teachings) due to himself.
Just as it is due to himself regarding what is lost from the Imam's discipline and his governance, in that he was forced to hide.
And if his fear were removed, he would appear.
So the grace of his governance would be realized for them, and what he has of concealed matters would become clear to them.
So if he does not do so and remains hidden, it is due to himself in both cases.
And this is strong, as the principles dictate.

key_terms.الْغَيْبَةِ: Occultation (Ghaybah), the state of concealment of the Imam
key_terms.الْمُرْتَضَى: Sayyid Murtadha, a prominent Shia scholar
key_terms.تَأْدِيبِ الْإِمَامِ: The Imam's discipline or educational governance

ai.seo_question: Why does the Imam's occultation not relieve people of religious obligations according to Sayyid Murtadha?
ai.summary: Sayyid al-Murtadha asserts that the Imam’s concealment (*ghayba*) does not negate the obligation of religious duty, as the loss of transmitted knowledge is attributed to the concealers rather than the Imam’s authority. He argues that if the threat forcing the Imam into hiding were removed, he would emerge to exercise direct governance (*tadbir*) and reveal hidden truths, thereby fulfilling the divine grace (*lutf*). This reasoning is grounded in Usuli principles, emphasizing that the Imam’s potential presence ensures the continuity of guidance despite the practical limitations imposed by his enemies.
